subject: Production timeouts & sudden p95/p99 regressions impacting FastCart checkout
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fastcart.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: payments-team@fastcart.com
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 15:12:08 -0700
Subject: Production timeouts and 429s impacting checkout - urgent

Sergio —

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 and p99 latency on the Redwood Hosted API for our checkout flow starting ~14:45 UTC. Customers are getting 429s and timeouts during payment authorization; we saw a ~7% drop in completed checkouts in the last 45 minutes.

Attached are a couple of screenshots from our monitoring and a request dump that shows repeated attempts for the same session IDs. This appears correlated with your API returning intermittent 429s followed by long tails on subsequent requests.

We need an immediate mitigation (either throttling guidance or temporary capacity) and an exec-level contact for escalation — this is revenue-impacting. Please advise the fastest path to stabilize.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Payments, FastCart

[Attachment: request-dump-20270417.json (application/json)]

— Sergio

A couple additional notes from our side:
- Impact window so far: ~14:45-15:35 UTC.
- We see aggressive client retries from mobile web instances (no exponential jitter, immediate retries x3). That pattern seems to magnify the number of in-flight requests after the first 429.
- This is hitting peak checkout traffic; every extra 200ms on p99 translates to ~$xxk/hour in lost conversions for us.

Please let me know if you’ll need someone from our infra team on the bridge. We need visibility to execs — I’ll escalate on my side too.

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fastcart.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 01:54:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts and 429s impacting checkout - urgent

Elena / team —

Initial engineering triage summary (quick findings):
- Timeline: We see a config rollout at 14:30 UTC yesterday that modified the global token-bucket parameters for the hosted API routing layer. The rollout reduced burst allowance to improve global fairness.
- FastCart traffic pattern: high-concurrency checkout bursts combined with client-side immediate retry loops (no exponential backoff) produced a high rate of retries after initial 429s.
- Observed effect: the combination of aggressive retries plus reduced burst allowance created a feedback loop where 429s triggered many near-simultaneous retries, increasing queue saturation and pushing p95/p99 latency much higher.
- Additional observations: increased worker CPU context switching and longer GC pauses on a subset of serving nodes correlated with the tail latency spikes.

Immediate mitigations we’ve applied or recommend (now -> 3 hours):
1) Temporary change: rollback the recent burst-reduction config for the affected routing pool (DONE at 01:40 UTC) to restore previous headroom.
2) Hotfix policy: enable per-customer token smoothing for project fastcart-prod-1 to avoid synchronized retries causing a single queue full.
3) Client guidance: ask FastCart to implement exponential backoff with capped jitter on retries (we can provide a small snippet).
4) Short-term capacity: spin additional hot replicas on the hosted pool for the us region (in progress).
5) Monitoring: added a p99-specific alert and a request-id tracing sample for impacted sessions.

Attachment: a short debug snapshot with the sample traces we pulled. This shows the retry amplification pattern for fc-req-8a3b.

Longer-term work: improve server-side retry smoothing and add automatic adaptive per-customer backpressure controls in the routing layer. I’ll open a follow-up engineering ticket (INF-8721) for the backlog.

— Michael
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
[Attachment: engineer-debug-snapshot.log (text/plain)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Team —

Summary: FastCart experienced a p95/p99 regression tied to a routing-layer burst config change plus client-side immediate retries. Michael rolled back the burst change, applied per-customer smoothing, and we are scaling additional replicas. Early indicators show conversion rates stabilizing but we’re keeping the bridge open.

Asks:
- Vivek: please approve a one-off credit for FastCart for the impacted window (support estimate attached) and join a 30-min exec call if available.
- Tessa: please prepare a short post-incident note for the customer that includes the immediate mitigations and the roadmap ticket (INF-8721).
- Monica/Michael: keep the hourly updates going until we confirm steady-state for 24h.

Elena — thank you for the quick signal and for providing request samples; we’ll follow up with the post-incident RCA and next steps. I’ll coordinate an exec call once Vivek confirms availability.

— Sergio
